records.deidentified_narrative: unit 2 (pedestrian) advised that she had been to atwoods, located at 5222 wesley, earlier in the day and had accidentally left her cell phone on the rear of her vehicle as she drove away from the store. unit 2 returned and began looking for the phone in the parking lot. when she could not find it she drove to the same exit she had used earlier in the day. while setting in her vehicle behind unit 2, she spotted her cell phone laying on the edge of the roadway (southwest corner). unit 1, a 3/4 ton diesel pick-up with a lift kit installed, was stopped at the exit of the parking lot, waiting to turn right (south) [roadway] (s. h. 34). because unit 1 is a larger pick up with a lift kit, it sets higher and thus limits visibility of the driver to see objects or persons on the passenger side. unit 2 exited her vehicle and walked along the passenger side of unit 1 to the edge of the roadway where she bent down to retrieve her cell phone. due to the height of the vehicle and the fact that unit 2 driver was focusing attention to approaching traffic to the left, unit 2 did not see unit 1 walking alongside his vehicle. as unit 2 bent down to retrieve the cell phone from the ground, unit 1 began to turn south (right) [roadway]. unit 1 struck unit 2 with its right side tires. unit 2 sustained apparent serious [medical facility] by american medical response. unit 1 driver remained on scene and rendered aid to unit 2 as well as awaited the arrival of emergency personnel. this crash occurred on the private parking lot of atwoods. unit 2 vehicle was not involved in the crash and is a non contact unit for the diagram. witnesses: colten porras @ [phone] & richard anderson @ [phone].

to set the vehicles cruise control when unit 1 left the roadway. while unit 1 was attempting to get back onto the roadway, it ran out of space and collided into the back of unit 2. the front passenger side bumper of unit 1 struck the rear drivers side of unit 2 in an angular direction. this caused unit 1 to sustain damage to its front bumper and to the passenger side of the vehicle. when unit 1 struck the rear of unit 2, it caused unit 2 and 3 to jack knife. during the jack knife, unit 4 was struck by unit 2 causing unit 4 to become airborne and land in the back of unit 2. unit 4 suffered serious bodily injuries. unit 5 was struck by both units 2 and 3 and caused unit 5 to become airborne. unit 5 landed on his back onto the ground, behind where unit 3 came to a rest. unit 5 also sustained serious bodily injuries. unit 1s wheel base, measured from outside of the tires tread, from tire to tire was 65. unit 1s right tire track where it left the roadway was located. the outside of that tire track to the roadway measured 93, which indicates that unit 1 left the roadway. the width of the tire track measured . 08 and unit 1s tires also measured . 08. the width of tires from units 2 and 3 measured . 06 showing the track width could only belonged to unit 1. the tire tracks for unit 2 were located. the wheel base of unit 2, measured from outside of the tires tread, from tire to tire was 85. the outside of that tire track to the roadway measured 78, which indicates that unit 2 was partially in the roadway . 09. unit 4 pedestrian originally parked units 2 and 3 in that location. unit 1 was a contributing factor to the crash because the driver [roadway]. unit 4 was also a contributing factor because he parked units 2 and 3 in the roadway. both units 1 and 4 are at fault.

records.deidentified_narrative: while standing at the above location which is the primary entrance into the b lot of the alamodome where covid 19 [roadway], unit # 2 a san antonio police officer was directing a vehicle into the second line of cars. i was standing next to a san antonio fire department golf cart that was making a supply run and had stopped next to me to await two more cars to turn in. suddenly the next car to turn in (unit # 1) did not turn but began to accelerate and missed the back of the turning in car. unit # 1 struck the officer (pedestrian 1) directing traffic knocking him onto the windshield and over the top of the car onto the pavement. i began yelling for the car to stop as it continued directly at myself and the safd golf cart. i back pedaled and continued to yell stop as unit # 1 struck unit # 3 the safd golf cart. unit # 1 pushed unit # 3 [roadway] continuing across the 3rd and 4th lines of entrance where it struck a large entrance sign and came to rest. i went to unit # 1 and turned the car off as it was still attempting to go with the driver pushing the gas pedal. once unit # 1 was shut off, i yelled to metro health and safd command personnel that i need paramedics to the entrance as a firefighter and police officer were down as the command trailer was just past the sign that was struck. firefighters came from the vaccination area and began treatment. on duty safd arrived and transported both the officer and firefighter to sammc via ambulances. i spoke with the driver of unit # 1 and he stated he only uses high blood pressure medication. he was checked by safd paramedics on scene and found to have no medical needs or injuries. when asked what had happened he stated he tried to take his foot off of the gas and his foot / leg would not move and kept pushing the gas which is why he swerved around the car turning in. once he was medically cleared, unit # 1 driver was given his first dose of vaccine and driven home. a medical advisory board form was completed and sent to dps on the driver of unit # 1. unit # 1 was towed by contract wrecker service to a body shop of his choosing.

off traffic, and ems was working on the pedestrian. the pedestrian was breathing but unresponsive, pedestrian [medical facility] and was accompanied by officer borja #1509. unit 1 was not at the location of the incident as they were not able to stop and render aid due to the high speed of traffic and the heavy amount of traffic on the roadway. once traffic was closed off from the roadway we were able to speak to witnesses. witnesses at the scene of the incident [roadway] barrier on [roadway] and [roadway], headed westbound as oncoming traffic was traveling northbound. witnesses stated that they had to take evasive action in order to not strike the pedestrian, but unit 1 was unable to avoid the collision with the pedestrian. witnesses then stated unit 1 [roadway] as they moved over [roadway] in order call 911 and wait for responding officers. while on scene, east patrol received a call from the driver of unit 1. officer carrion was the responding officer and was able to take the statement from the driver on unit 1 and awaited at the secondary location until we were able to make it out to his location. uedi pianfetti #2431 documented the damage to unit 1. supervisor sgt. chavez #3301 was notified of the incident as well as tid and csi in order to interview the witnesses and document the area. after tid, detective salazar #2260 had interviewed the witnesses at the primary location, and csi d. sarabia #9449, finished processing the scene, [roadway] and proceeded to the secondary location where unit 1 was located. upon arriving to the secondary location, officer svetlana #0608 had relieved officer carrion and was waiting with the driver of unit 1. officer carrion had taken the statement of the driver of unit 1. unit 1 driver stated he was traveling in the number 2 lane to the left and was behind a pickup truck. unit 1 driver saw the truck suddenly brake and swerve to the right. unit 1 driver also hit his brakes and swerved left. unit 1 driver said he hit what he believed to be a person. the collision caused left front quadrant damage to unit 1. unit 1 driver stated he moved over to the shoulder and called his wife. unit 1 driver said he exited the highways and attempted to turn around and go back to the scene. driver claimed ems and police were at the scene and he was not able to get back to the scene. unit 1 driver called 911 and was advised to pull over and police would be sent to him. unit 1 driver stopped at [roadway]. the driver of unit 1 was able to called 911 and report the collision as promptly as he could and was told by the dispatcher to await at a secondary location until officers could arrive. responding officers were able to interview the driver of unit 1 along with tid. unit 1 was still operable and the driver did not suffer any injuries. tid interviewed driver and collected his statement. tid advised officers to fill out a crash investigation. coban and bwc available

records.deidentified_narrative: on friday, march 22, 2021, at approximately 1815 hours, i officer b. kervin unit# 3419, of the new caney isd police department was notified by phone from officer a. ferretis #3408 of a mva involving a pedestrian at don ford staduim, new caney, texas in montgomery county. unit 1, owned by sanders, marquitta(tx dl [identifier]), a 2016 chevy malibu silver in color with ga lp,wqn 490, vin# 1g1zb5st1gf192101. unit#1 was sitting in a handicapped parking spot on the north side of don ford stadium. the owner of unit#1 had left to go inside the stadium and left her daughter, sanders, trinity dob [date],(student id# 21722) unattended in the car. during this time sanders, trinity started to get cold and moved over to the driver side and started the car, during this time the car got put into reverse and the car went backwards hitting a female pedestrian who was walking behind the car. then sanders, trinity got out of the vehicle and ran to find her mom, officer ladwig #3405 then was notified and made contact with the injured pedestrian, who was identified as jackson, jada simone tx dl [identifier], dob [date]. officer ladwig then radioed for ems, jackson, jada was complaining of right arm and right side pain but had no scratches, no brushing or any visible injuries. she was up standing and talking when officer ladwig arrived. medic 53 arrived and took jackson, [medical facility]. pictures were then taken of the scene and uploaded to the report, a citation ([identifier]) was issued for leaving a child in a vehicle unattended to unit#1 owner sanders, marquitta. there was property damage done to the fence and a handicapped sign was ran over.

(a) a pedestrian shall yield the right-of-way [roadway] if [roadway]:(1) other than in a marked crosswalk or in an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection; or(2) where a pedestrian tunnel or overhead pedestrian crossing has been provided.(b) between adjacent intersections at which traffic control signals are in operation, a pedestrian may cross only in a marked crosswalk.(c) a pedestrian may cross a roadway intersection diagonally only if and in the manner authorized by a traffic control device. there was no evidence at the scene that indicated unit 1 violated any provisions of the texas transportation code and displayed no signs of intoxication when interviewed at the scene. two additional witnesses were located which are harris county public health animal control officer allison post and kyle shelton. additionally, body worn camera footage from deputy d. bailey-tillman captured the crash and clearly indicates that unit 2 (watkins) violated the above provision of the texas transportation code. [case id]***(update [date])-determination of vehicle speed. after completing my scene and follow-up investigation of this crash, i used the evidence collected to determine the impact speed of the lincoln navigator driven by william faulkenberry. my review of this crash included, but was not limited to, the video of the crash captured by the body worn camera of deputy d. bailey-tillman who was running behind the pedestrian marlon watkins. i was able to observe watkins who was fleeing on foot from deputy bailey-tillman after assaulting a female complainant. after climbing a wrought iron fence, watkins ran into the roadway in the path of the lincoln [roadway] [roadway]. watkins was immediately struck by the front right of the lincoln navigator. the body worn camera video confirms that the leading edge of the lincoln navigator struck watkins below his center of mass. the result of this impact resulted in watkins legs being lifted off of the ground and the upper torso wrapping onto the vehicle`s hood. after impacting the hood, watkins is projected forward. this is defined as a wrap trajectory with watkins leaving the vehicle at an unknown angle greater than 0 degrees. i was also able to determine the total throw distance of watkins. i used the video to locate the area of impact. i then measured from this point to [roadway] left by the sliding body of watkins as it came to rest. this distance is 85`. i then used the searle pedestrian formula to calculate the approximate speed of the lincoln navigator. searle provides two equations with the first resulting in a maximum speed and is for a forward projection with a 0 degree angle of take-off for watkins. this is a wrap trajectory and this equation would be over estimating the speed of the vehicle as the take-off angle was greater than 0 degrees. the searle maximum equation solves for the velocity. using the total throw distance of 85` and the drag factor of . 66, recommended by searle for this equation, results in a velocity for the lincoln navigator of 60. 1 fps or 41 mph. the lincoln navigator would have been traveling at a speed lower than 41 mph due to this not being a forward projection. i then used the searle minimum formula which is derived with a departure angle of 33. 4 degrees when using the searle drag factor of . 66. this results in a velocity of 50. 16 fps or 34 mph for the lincoln navigator. based on my investigation of this crash, the speed of the lincoln driven by william faulkenberry was approximately 34-41 mph in a posted 45 mph speed zone and not a factor in this crash and not a violation of the texas transportation code. end of supplement, [case id].

records.public_safe_text: unit 1 was [roadway] at [roadway]. unit 2 is a pedestrian that was fleeing (running) from a uniformed deputy sheriff under hcso event [identifier]. unit 2 jumped a large metal fence and [roadway] which was occupied by unit 1. unit 2 entered into the direct path of unit 1 and the front right of unit 1 struck unit 2. unit 2 was transported to [medical facility] (katy) due to injuries sustained in [medical facility]. witnesses: harris county sheriff's deputy d. bailey-tillman & deputy g. davilla. this [case id] under investigation by the vehicular crimes division of the harris county sheriff's office. ***update [date], the harris county institute of forensic sciences ([case id]) ruled as the manner of death: ""accident - mva (pedestrian)"" and as the cause of death: ""multiple blunt force injuries"" for unit 2 (watkins). the toxicology laboratory results also indicated that watkins had no alcohol and no drugs in his system at the time of his death. unit 2 (watkins) failed to yield right of way to unit 1 [roadway] at a point other than a crosswalk and violated the texas transportation code: sec. 552. 005. crossing at point other than crosswalk. (a) a pedestrian shall yield the right-of-way [roadway] if [roadway]:(1) other than in a marked crosswalk or in an unmarked crosswalk at an intersection; or(2) where a pedestrian tunnel or overhead pedestrian crossing has been provided.(b) between adjacent intersections at which traffic control signals are in operation, a pedestrian may cross only in a marked crosswalk.(c) a pedestrian may cross a roadway intersection diagonally only if and in the manner authorized by a traffic control device. there was no evidence at the scene that indicated unit 1 violated any provisions of the texas transportation code and displayed no signs of intoxication when interviewed at the scene. two additional witnesses were located which are harris county public health animal control officer allison post and kyle shelton. additionally, body worn camera footage from deputy d. bailey-tillman captured the crash and clearly indicates that unit 2 (watkins) violated the above provision of the texas transportation code. [case id]***(update [date])-determination of vehicle speed. after completing my scene and follow-up investigation of this crash, i used the evidence collected to determine the impact speed of the lincoln navigator driven by william faulkenberry. my review of this crash included, but was not limited to, the video of the crash captured by the body worn camera of deputy d. bailey-tillman who was running behind the pedestrian marlon watkins. i was able to observe watkins who was fleeing on foot from deputy bailey-tillman after assaulting a female complainant. after climbing a wrought iron fence, watkins ran into the roadway in the path of the lincoln [roadway] [roadway]. watkins was immediately struck by the front right of the lincoln navigator. the body worn camera video confirms that the leading edge of the lincoln navigator struck watkins below his center of mass. the result of this impact resulted in watkins legs being lifted off of the ground and the upper torso wrapping onto the vehicle`s hood. after impacting the hood, watkins is projected forward. this is defined as a wrap trajectory with watkins leaving the vehicle at an unknown angle greater than 0 degrees. i was also able to determine the total throw distance of watkins. i used the video to locate the area of impact. i then measured from this point to [roadway] left by the sliding body of watkins as it came to rest. this distance is 85`. i then used the searle pedestrian formula to calculate the approximate speed of the lincoln navigator. searle provides two equations with the first resulting in a maximum speed and is for a forward projection with a 0 degree angle of take-off for watkins. this is a wrap trajectory and this equation would be over estimating the speed of the vehicle as the take-off angle was greater than 0 degrees. the searle maximum equation solves for the velocity. using the total throw distance of 85` and the drag factor of . 66, recommended by searle for this equation, results in a velocity for the lincoln navigator of 60. 1 fps or 41 mph. the lincoln navigator would have been traveling at a speed lower than 41 mph due to this not being a forward projection. i then used the searle minimum formula which is derived with a departure angle of 33. 4 degrees when using the searle drag factor of . 66. this results in a velocity of 50. 16 fps or 34 mph for the lincoln navigator. based on my investigation of this crash, the speed of the lincoln driven by william faulkenberry was approximately 34-41 mph in a posted 45 mph speed zone and not a factor in this crash and not a violation of the texas transportation code. end of supplement, [case id].
